title: Acceptable Encryption Standard
definition: Ciphers in use must meet or exceed the sets defined as "AES-compatible" or "partially AES-compatible" in the IETF/IRTF Cipher Catalog, or the set defined for use in NIST FIPS 140-2 or any superseding document applicable on the implementation date.

title: Acceptable Encryption Standard
definition: The Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) is strongly recommended for symmetric encryption.

title: Acceptable Encryption Standard
definition: Algorithms in use must meet the standards defined for use in NIST FIPS 140-2 or any superseding document applicable on the implementation date.

title: Acceptable Encryption Standard
definition: RSA and Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC) are strongly recommended for asymmetric encryption.

title: Acceptable Encryption Standard
definition: ECDSA signatures must use a minimum key length of P-256.

title: Acceptable Encryption Standard
definition: Consider RFC 6090 to avoid patent infringement when using ECDSA.

title: Acceptable Encryption Standard
definition: RSA signatures must use a minimum key length of 2048 bits.

title: Acceptable Encryption Standard
definition: RSA signatures must use a secure padding scheme.

title: Acceptable Encryption Standard
definition: The PKCS#7 padding scheme is recommended for RSA signatures.

title: Acceptable Encryption Standard
definition: Message hashing is required for RSA signatures.

title: Acceptable Encryption Standard
definition: LDWM signatures must use SHA-256 and refer to the LDWM Hash-based Signatures Draft.

title: Acceptable Encryption Standard
definition: The organization must adhere to the NIST Policy on Hash Functions.

title: Acceptable Encryption Standard
definition: Key exchanges must use Diffie-Hellman, IKE, or Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman (ECDH).

title: Acceptable Encryption Standard
definition: Endpoints must be authenticated before session keys are exchanged or derived.

title: Acceptable Encryption Standard
definition: Public keys used to establish trust must be authenticated before use.

title: Acceptable Encryption Standard
definition: Public-key authentication may include transmission through a cryptographically signed message or manual verification of the public-key hash.

title: Acceptable Encryption Standard
definition: All authentication servers, such as RADIUS or TACACS servers, must have a valid certificate signed by a known trusted provider installed.

title: Acceptable Encryption Standard
definition: All servers and applications using SSL or TLS must have certificates signed by a known, trusted provider.

title: Acceptable Encryption Standard
definition: Cryptographic keys must be generated and stored securely to prevent loss, theft, or compromise.

title: Acceptable Encryption Standard
definition: Key generation must be seeded by an industry-standard random number generator (RNG).
